title: Fire leaves over 100 families homeless in Mohakhali's Sattola slum
excerpt: The slum has burned at least six times before since 2012. Some residents say fires have been set on purpose in disputes over the land.

image.alt: Tin and plastic shanties along a lake in a Dhaka slum
image.credit: SuSanA Secretariat / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0

content:
A fire on Wednesday morning (18 November) left more than 100 families homeless in the Sattola slum in Mohakhali, Dhaka, bdnews24.com's Bangla edition reported. Eight fire service units fought the blaze. The first arrived at 10:10am and the fire was brought under control at 11:15am. No one was reported hurt.

Lt Col Mohammad Mahmudul Hasan, Director (Operations and Maintenance) of the Fire Service, said the cause was not yet known and an investigation committee would be formed.

A slum that keeps burning

Sattola also caught fire in 2012, 2015, 2016, 2020, 2021 and 2025, the paper said. It pointed to illegal electricity and gas connections, and to residents' claims that some fires have been set on purpose in disputes over the land. The report did not mention any relief for the families.

Why it matters

Families who lose their homes in slum fires often lose savings, documents and school materials too, and many rent rather than own, so they get little help. Urban poverty, shelter and child protection NGOs in Dhaka may be needed for emergency support, and the repeated fires point to unsafe wiring and insecure tenure that city authorities have not fixed.

What to watch

Relief from the city corporation or district administration, the findings of the investigation committee, and whether families are allowed to rebuild.
